rules.title: Annual General Adjustment capped at 5% (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: In a fully covered Berkeley unit, your landlord may raise the rent each year only by the Annual General Adjustment set by the Rent Board. The adjustment follows a CPI formula and can never be more than 5%. A landlord who has unused (banked) adjustments from earlier years may still raise rent by more than 5%, but only up to the rent ceiling.
rules.key_value: AGA tied to CPI, maximum 5% per year
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully covered units: most units in multifamily properties built before 1980, plus certain single-family homes (tenancies that began before 1996, or 5+ rooms rented out individually). Government-owned or subsidized units (Section 8, Shelter Plus Care, VASH, LIHTC, HOME, etc.) are now fully covered when the unit type is fully covered and no federal or state law bars rent control.
rules.exemptions: New construction (certificate of occupancy issued after 1980), most single-family homes and most condominiums are only partially covered, with no rent ceiling. Section 202/811 units and some HUD-mortgage project-based subsidy units are partially covered. Units where the tenant shares a kitchen or bath with the landlord are exempt only if the landlord lived on the property at the start of the tenancy.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance (B.M.C. Ch. 13.76), as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.

exemption_tests.description: New construction with a certificate of occupancy issued after 1980 is only partially covered (no rent ceiling)
Tenant shares a kitchen or bath with the landlord, and the landlord lived on the property at the start of the tenancy
Subsidized units where federal or state law bars rent control (Section 202, Section 811, and project-based subsidies with HUD-insured or HUD-held mortgages) are only partially covered

rules.conflict_note: The page describes the construction cutoff two ways: 'built before 1980' and 'certificate of occupancy issued after 1980'. The exact cutoff date in the ordinance is not given here, so 1980-12-31 is an approximation. State Costa-Hawkins limits rent control on newer construction and single-family homes, and federal law preempts it for some subsidized units. Where the unit is fully covered, Berkeley rent control governs instead of the state cap (Civ. Code 1947.12). The page gives no effective date for Measure BB.

rules.title: Capital improvement rent increase petitions only for completed work
rules.requirement: A landlord may petition the Rent Board for a rent increase only for capital improvements that are already finished. A landlord can no longer get increases approved in advance for planned improvements.
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully covered rental units subject to rent ceilings.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (B.M.C. Ch. 13.76), as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: Landlords can only file a petition for rent increases for completed capital improvements (they can no longer petition to have rent increases preliminarily authorized for planned capital improvements).

rules.title: Just cause required for eviction from fully or partially covered units
rules.requirement: If your Berkeley unit is fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance, your landlord cannot evict you without one of the just causes listed in the ordinance.
rules.coverage_conditions: All fully and partially covered units. This includes post-1980 new construction, single-family homes, condos and, under Measure BB, government-owned or subsidized units.
rules.exemptions: Fully exempt units, such as a unit where the tenant shares a kitchen or bath with a landlord who lived on the property before the tenancy began.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (B.M.C. § 13.76.130), as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)

exemption_tests.description: Tenant shares a kitchen or bath with the landlord, and the landlord lived on the property at the start of the tenancy

rules.title: No eviction for nonpayment below one month's Fair Market Rent
rules.requirement: Your landlord can evict you for unpaid rent only if you owe at least one month of HUD Fair Market Rent for a unit of your size in the Oakland-Fremont metro area, for the fiscal year the rent is demanded.
rules.key_value: Rent debt must be at least 1 month of HUD Fair Market Rent (Oakland-Fremont)
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (B.M.C. § 13.76.130), as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR

rules.title: No eviction for refusing to sign a substantially similar new lease
rules.requirement: When your fixed-term lease ends, your landlord cannot evict you for refusing to sign a new, substantially similar lease.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (B.M.C. § 13.76.130), as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease upon expiration of a fixed-term lease.

rules.title: Stricter requirements for evictions based on lease violations
rules.requirement: An eviction for breaking the lease must be based on a lease term you agreed to, and the violation must cause the landlord substantial, actual harm. The landlord must show your behavior was unreasonable. Before serving an eviction notice, the landlord must give you a notice to stop that names the lease term and describes the violation and the harm.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (B.M.C. § 13.76.130), as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: The landlord’s notice to the tenant to stop the violation (which is required before the landlord can serve an eviction notice) must specify the lease term, and describe the violation and resulting harm in enough detail for a reasonable person to understand.

rules.title: Eviction notice content and filing with the Rent Board within 3 business days
rules.requirement: Any termination notice must say that advice is available from the Rent Board and give its phone number and website. The landlord must file copies of termination notices, notices to quit, and summons and complaints with the Rent Board within three business days of serving you.
rules.key_value: File with the Rent Board within 3 business days
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (B.M.C. § 13.76.130), as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: The landlord must file with the Rent Board a copy of any notice to terminate a tenancy, notice to quit, and summons and complaint no later than three business days after the tenant was served with the document.

rules.title: Mandatory yearly inflation adjustment of owner move-in relocation payments
rules.requirement: If you are evicted so the owner can move in, you are entitled to relocation assistance. The Rent Board must raise the amount for inflation every year.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants in covered units facing owner move-in evictions.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance (B.M.C. Ch. 13.76), as amended by Measure BB (Nov. 2024)
rules.quoted_span: The Rent Board must make inflationary adjustments to owner move-in eviction relocation assistance amounts each year.

notes: The page says Measure BB passed in November 2024 but never gives its effective date, so effective_date is null on every record. The only related dates are that the Notice of Tenant Rights applies to tenancies starting on or after 2024-12-20 and the utility rule applies to tenancies starting on or after 2024-02-06. The page does not give section numbers. I cited the ordinance as B.M.C. Ch. 13.76, with § 13.76.130 for just cause, from general knowledge, so please check them. Four items were left out as out of scope: the Notice of Tenant Rights, utility billing, the tenant right to organize, and the tenancy registration fines. Subsidized-unit coverage is folded into the coverage of the 5% Annual General Adjustment record. The 1980 construction cutoff is approximate because the page calls it 'built before 1980' in one place and 'certificate of occupancy issued after 1980' in another.
